$schema: self-describing snapshot of the whole project; keep in sync with the .md files

project.name: competitor-pricing-monitor
project.objective: Daily Booking.com rate-shopping for StayVista: scrape 30 nights of forward rates for each StayVista property and its nearby competitors, and surface where StayVista is mispriced.
project.phase: hardening — CSV is now the single source of truth; new 6-property Goa set resolved, geolocated and being scanned for competitors

stack: Google Sheets (Apps Script Web App or service account)

keyModules.name: refresh.js
keyModules.purpose: Harvest Booking.com cookies via Playwright, then scrape 30 nights x property x room at 80-way fetch concurrency with adaptive throttling.

keyModules.name: import-properties.js
keyModules.purpose: Parse properties.csv into config/properties.json; collapse multi-unit rows; attach manual competitors; invoke discovery.

keyModules.name: discover.js
keyModules.purpose: Full Booking.com market scan per property (city search + lat/lng search, API interception, cumulative cache).

keyModules.name: serve.js
keyModules.purpose: Static dashboard + ~30 JSON endpoints, SSE progress channels, spawns the other scripts as child processes.

keyModules.name: discovery-engine
keyModules.purpose: Weighted 8-factor competitor relevance scoring with hard rejection rules.

keyModules.name: pricing-rows
keyModules.purpose: Single source of truth for Google Sheets column order, row building and the change-detection hash.

keyModules.name: chrome
keyModules.purpose: Cross-platform Chrome discovery and CDP launch; headless except for refresh.js which needs a visible login window.

keyModules.name: holidays
keyModules.purpose: Indian holiday table 2025-2028 and long-weekend derivation, used for night typing.

keyModules.name: geocode
keyModules.purpose: Nominatim geocoding with a persistent file cache plus haversine distance.

keyModules.name: dashboard
keyModules.purpose: 7 panel single-file SPA: Overview, Calendar, Long Weekends, Analysis, Suggestions, Discover (Leaflet map), History.

patterns: properties.csv is the authoritative property list; config/properties.json is a derived cache that accumulates and must be filtered against the CSV
Playwright is used only to obtain cookies; the hot path is raw fetch() for speed

Inventory state machine: classifyProbe / delistCandidates / applyVerdict / reconcileTracked / purgeableIds. Only a 404/410 delists; every ambiguous signal keeps the property. All id comparisons canonicalised (pool uses hyphens, config uses underscores).

decisions.decision: Resolve share links by following the redirect, and take coordinates from the Booking.com property page rather than a Nominatim name lookup.
decisions.rationale: A plain redirect-follow recovers the canonical /hotel/in/<slug> URL, which unblocks import, scraping AND identity checks at once. Coordinates then come from the listing itself (JSON-LD geo), which is authoritative — a Nominatim guess on a name like "Studio 109 Apartment by tisyastays" would be unreliable. A bare fetch of the property page is not enough: Booking.com returns a 202 bot-check stub, so the page must be loaded in Chrome.

decisions.decision: properties.csv is the single source of truth for which properties exist; the dashboard selector is driven from a live parse of it, not from config/properties.json.
decisions.rationale: config accumulates: an import run with --property=<id> preserves every other entry, so IDs deleted from the CSV survive in config and latest.dashboard.json forever. 307 such orphans were showing in the dropdown.

decisions.decision: An empty CSV means zero properties, not 'unknown' — the dropdown blanks. Only an unreachable server or malformed reply falls back to the configured list.
decisions.rationale: User explicitly required that clearing the sheet clears the dropdown. Tracked with a separate CSV_LOADED flag rather than inferring from set size.

decisions.decision: Column B (Property) is the authoritative dropdown label, and scraped data only carries over to a CSV row when the row's Booking slug matches the config entry's slug.
decisions.rationale: Property IDs are reused across sheet revisions. The new CSV numbers rows 1-6, colliding with old IDs 1 (Backspace Anjuna Beach) and 5 (The Boulevard Villa) — without this guard those old names and prices would appear under the new property names.

Booking.com cookies from a logged-in Chrome profile are needed for reliable price data
Booking.com page structure (the b_rooms_available_and_soldout JSON blob) stays stable
Everything runs locally on Windows against a user-visible Chrome; there is no server deployment

lessonsLearned: A themed app has no hardcoded surface colours — text and the surface behind it must come from the same theme, or one moves without the other (BUG-015)
A rendering sweep cannot catch a contrast bug: the DOM is perfect and only the pixels are wrong. Assert the invariant at the token level instead
A guard you cannot see fail is not a guard — reintroduce the bug and confirm the check goes red before trusting it
var() is resolved by the CSS engine, never by a canvas: Chart.js silently ignores an unparseable colour and keeps the previous one (BUG-017)
A placeholder written in markup needs an owner on EVERY path that can reach it, including the error paths where a stale "Loading..." is most misleading (BUG-016)
inferPrice() is not evidence a night exists — it answers "what would this plausibly cost", not "what did Booking.com quote" (BUG-009)
Rendering a panel must never start a scrape (BUG-010)
A zero computed from an empty input is not a measurement — return null and render "—" with a reason (BUG-012)
Absence from a scan is not evidence a listing is gone: Booking.com hides properties with no availability for the probed night
config/properties.json is a cache, not a source of truth — always reconcile it against properties.csv
Property IDs are reused across CSV revisions; the Booking.com slug is the only reliable identity for a listing
Never re-implement the CSV parser — lib/csv-properties.js is the one implementation and tests pin it (D-006)
Reports must compute every name and number they state; build-price-report.js hardcoded a former ID 1 hostel competitors and asserted them for a villa (D-007)
Booking.com ss= text search is intermittent, not broken — so candidate pool sizes are not comparable between scans
schtasks /TR does not run through a shell: >> log 2>&1 written there becomes argv and redirects nothing
Excel locks properties.csv while open; writes from Node fail with EBUSY
properties.csv is Windows-1252 — decode strict UTF-8 first, then fall back, or names become mojibake
Leaflet L.latLng() returns null for malformed coordinates instead of throwing, so bad data surfaces later from inside the library
A bare fetch cannot read a Booking.com property page (HTTP 202 bot-check stub); page metadata needs the browser, prices do not
Writing tests for a contract you think is settled finds real bugs — the CSV tests immediately exposed lossy escaped-quote handling

Absence from a discovery scan is NOT evidence of delisting: the scan probes one night and Booking.com hides unavailable properties, so 12 of 24 absent properties were all live on direct probe. Only a 404 on the property page delists.
config/properties.json has five uncoordinated read-modify-writers, so concurrent runs silently lose changes — never scan while the dashboard is in use
Analysis thresholds must be relative to the property ADR — the portfolio spans 6x, so any fixed rupee threshold means something different at each end
A least-squares slope without R2 is not a trend; weekday/weekend oscillation alone produces a non-zero slope
Math.round(null*100) is 0, so every unmodelled value rendered as a confident zero until each was made explicitly nullable
Absence from a scan must be scope-aware: 763 of property 1s pool were out of the scans reach, not gone
pkill -f <port> never matches a server whose port comes from an env var — kill by PID or you test stale code
